claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has usable high-temperature strength.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance and suffers pesting.
Pack cementation in an Al-rich powder pack at 900–950 °C for 2–4 hours will enrich the alloy surface in aluminum.
The aluminization treatment will produce a thin, uniform Al-enriched surface layer.
During oxidation, the Al-enriched layer will convert into a continuous and adherent Al2O3 scale.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a barrier to further oxygen ingress.
Restricting oxygen ingress with the Al2O3 scale will prevent pesting during a 5-hour exposure to air at 800 °C.
The surface treatment will leave the bulk microstructure largely unaffected.
Aluminized material will have markedly better oxygen resistance than untreated material.
Aluminized material will retain room-temperature tensile properties comparable to untreated material.
Aluminized material will retain high-temperature yield strength comparable to untreated material at about 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Thermal cycling or mechanical loading may cause a brittle or poorly adherent Al2O3 scale to spall.
Spallation of the Al2O3 scale would compromise the expected oxidation protection.

contradictions.description: The conditions field places the 800 °C oxidation exposure under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1, whereas the experiment describes oxidation first and applies those strain rates only during subsequent high-temperature mechanical testing.
